newsitem.title: UK: Eurobond supply ceases amid May Day holidays.
newsitem.headline: Eurobond supply ceases amid May Day holidays.

text.p: The May Day holiday which closed markets in many key centres on Thursday saw primary market supply dry up.
"It is going to be extremely quiet today and on Friday," a syndicate manager said.
Markets are closed in among other countries Argentina, Austria, Belgium, Bulgaria, Colombia, Ecuador, Germany, Mexico, Russia, Switzerland and Venezuela.
The British election also contributed to the lack of supply, dealers said, but added demand for sterling Eurobonds looked set to improve afterwards.
Financial markets have already factored in a victory by the Labour Party, well ahead in opinion polls, and an interest rate hike of either 25 or 50 basis points, they said.

Spreads on both the long and short end were holding steady but, they said, there appeared to be more scope for spreads to tighten on the short end because of sterling, which is holding near four-year highs against the mark.

The currency generally is expected to maintain its strength, largely because it is the one most likely to opt out of the European currency union in the first wave of European Economic and Monetary Union (EMU) in 1999.

Syndicate sources said new issues could emerge from the British utility sector later this year if the Labour Party won the election and levied a larger-than-expected windfall tax. They said some may fund the windfall tax through new issues, which typically are dated 10 years or longer.
